study.title: From review text to guest segments
study.summary: Language analysis builds the features; clustering tests how reviews group together.

nodes.label: Review text
nodes.detail: 74,896 reviews across 458 Da Nang hotels. The unit represented in the segmentation is a review, not a verified unique guest.

nodes.label: Aspect sentiment
nodes.detail: Map sentences to hotel attributes and score sentiment at that level. Project materials report 148,846 aspect–sentence pairs; they do not identify a specific ABSA checkpoint.

nodes.label: K-means
nodes.detail: Group reviews by similarity in attribute-level features. Ten reported groups form the displayed segmentation; the portfolio does not contain the full selection diagnostics.

nodes.label: Gaussian mixture
nodes.detail: Check the segmentation with a probabilistic alternative. Agreement scores and covariance settings are not supplied, so this is a reported robustness step rather than a reproduced test.

nodes.label: Guest profiles
nodes.detail: Compare what each group emphasizes, then name the profiles. The labels summarize priorities visible in the review features.

study.legend: Arrows show the analysis sequence, not causal effects.

next.title: Test whether the segments travel
next.summary: Develop a reproducible NLP and clustering benchmark before applying profiles to new hotels.

nodes.label: Annotated reviews
nodes.detail: Create a stratified human-labelled subset covering languages, hotel classes and positive and negative reviews. Keep annotator agreement and uncertain labels visible.

nodes.label: Embedding + ABSA
nodes.detail: Compare the existing attribute features with multilingual sentence embeddings and a sentiment model. Fine-tuning is conditional on enough labelled examples; no checkpoint has been trained here.

nodes.label: K-means / GMM
nodes.detail: Compare cluster counts, feature scaling and covariance choices. Consider HDBSCAN only if uneven density or outliers make the existing partition unsuitable.

nodes.label: Unseen hotels + dates
nodes.detail: Reserve hotels and a later time window. Examine cluster stability, semantic coherence and assignment uncertainty, not just a visually neat two-dimensional plot.

nodes.label: Service trial
nodes.detail: Use validated profiles to choose one service intervention. Test guest outcomes with a separate design; cluster membership alone does not show that an intervention works.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Do the same service priorities remain visible in unseen hotels and later reviews?
Design & unit
Model-development study using reviews nested within hotels; retain hotel and date identifiers for validation.
Measures & analysis
Audit aspect and sentiment labels, benchmark feature representations and clustering, then report stability and uncertain assignments.
Data & sample
Requires the review matrix, collection dates, feature codebook and reuse permission. Set annotation size from class coverage and target precision; do not treat 10 clusters as a fixed requirement.
Decision gate
Extend only if the patterns are stable and interpretable in the reserved data. A service pilot needs its own outcome, comparison and sample rationale.

study.title: Three ways to model the same choices
study.summary: Each model answers a different question about preference differences.

nodes.label: Choice tasks
nodes.detail: 212 validated young consumers compared vehicle profiles. Repeated tasks belong to the same respondent; they are not independent new consumers.

nodes.label: Multinomial logit
nodes.detail: Estimate a shared utility specification as a baseline. Price and vehicle features enter the choice model; the archive does not provide a complete comparison table.

nodes.label: Mixed logit
nodes.detail: Allow preferences to vary across people rather than imposing one coefficient vector. Distribution and simulation settings require the full estimation specification.

nodes.label: Latent class
nodes.detail: Represent preference differences with two reported groups: 65% utility-focused and 35% design-sensitive. These are model-based groups rather than observed market shares.

nodes.label: Willingness to pay
nodes.detail: Express feature trade-offs relative to price, with intervals. The displayed values come from the reported latent class model and summarize stated preferences in the task design.

study.legend: Arrows show the analysis sequence, not causal effects.

next.title: From explanation to held-out choice prediction
next.summary: Keep interpretable choice models as the benchmark; add ML only if it improves a genuine prediction task.

nodes.label: Recover task design
nodes.detail: Recover alternatives, coding, price units, respondent IDs and the experimental design. Reproduce the existing utility and willingness-to-pay calculations first.

nodes.label: Logit + boosted trees
nodes.detail: Compare the choice specifications with a choice-set-aware boosted-tree ranking baseline. Each prediction must account for all alternatives available in that task.

nodes.label: Respondent holdout
nodes.detail: Keep every task from a respondent in one fold. Compare held-out choice log loss, probability calibration and uncertainty; fit preprocessing only within training folds.

nodes.label: New buyer sample
nodes.detail: Test transportability with a separately recruited buyer sample. Observed purchase follow-up would be a distinct outcome; do not equate intention, stated choice and purchase.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Can the estimated preferences predict choices for consumers outside the estimation sample?
Design & unit
Prediction benchmark using respondent-grouped validation, followed by an independently collected sample.
Measures & analysis
Compare choice probabilities and calibration. Preserve logit-based willingness-to-pay interpretation separately from tree predictions.
Data & sample
Requires the full task-level data and model code. Budget the external sample against the desired precision in held-out performance and subgroup estimates.
Decision gate
Keep the simpler model unless prediction improves consistently. A pricing experiment needs observed demand and a separate causal design.

study.title: Message, appeal and purchase intention
study.summary: The 2 × 2 experiment separates manipulated cues from the measured moderator.

nodes.label: Argument quality
nodes.detail: High and low argument quality define one experimental factor. The supplied stimulus set supports this contrast; no additional conditions are introduced.

nodes.label: Peripheral appeal
nodes.detail: Appeal is the second experimental factor. The framework includes social attractiveness, physical attractiveness and attitude similarity.

nodes.label: Purchase intention
nodes.detail: Compare intention across the four stimulus conditions. The outcome is a stated response, not an observed transaction.

nodes.label: Speciesism
nodes.detail: Examine whether the response to virtual endorsers differs with stronger human preference. Speciesism is measured rather than randomized.

study.legend: Solid arrows show cue–outcome relationships; dashed arrows point to the relationships moderated by speciesism.

next.title: Test disclosure alongside persuasion
next.summary: Extend the experiment to the decision a brand actually faces: how clearly to identify a virtual creator.

nodes.label: Disclosure × message
nodes.detail: Randomize disclosure clarity and message quality with matched creative assets. Pretest comprehension and keep the product, creator exposure and layout comparable.

nodes.label: Trust + recognition
nodes.detail: Measure recognition of the virtual creator and trust after exposure. Mediation remains conditional on temporal ordering and identification assumptions.

nodes.label: Click or product choice
nodes.detail: Record a prespecified voluntary click or incentive-compatible choice. Report intention as a separate secondary outcome.

nodes.label: Human preference
nodes.detail: Retain the measured moderator, define interaction tests before collection and avoid splitting a continuous score just to obtain a stronger result.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Does clearer virtual-creator disclosure change behavior, and does the effect vary with human preference?
Design & unit
Preregistered factorial experiment with participants randomly assigned to matched posts.
Measures & analysis
Primary randomized contrast on behavior; secondary intention, trust and recognition. Specify interactions and multiplicity before data collection.
Data & sample
Requires new stimuli and participants. Use a smallest meaningful main effect and interaction to plan sample size; pilot the measures first.
Decision gate
Report the randomized contrast separately from measured mechanisms. Use real purchase claims only if transactions are observed.

study.title: Knowledge and activity in the same model
study.summary: Regression separates adjusted associations from the descriptive knowledge scores.

nodes.label: Nutrition knowledge
nodes.detail: The adapted 20-item CoNKS scale measures correct nutrition-knowledge responses. Its score enters the regression alongside activity and the demographic covariates.

nodes.label: Physical activity
nodes.detail: Activity is expressed in MET-minutes per week. Its adjusted association is evaluated alongside knowledge, age and sex.

nodes.label: Age + sex
nodes.detail: The reported regression includes age and sex. Adjustment does not remove all possible confounding or establish time order.

nodes.label: Multiple regression
nodes.detail: The reported model has R² = 0.538 in the student sample. This is explanatory fit in the supplied analysis, not a held-out prediction score.

nodes.label: Diet-quality score
nodes.detail: Dietary responses provide the modeled outcome. Diversity, protective-food and food-to-limit scores remain distinct measures.

study.legend: Arrows show model inputs and outcome; this cross-sectional model does not establish causation.

next.title: Can prediction identify a useful intervention?
next.summary: Build a small, auditable prediction benchmark before testing nutrition support.

nodes.label: Repeated diet measures
nodes.detail: Collect repeated dietary responses with prespecified recall windows. Record the timing of knowledge, activity and outcome measures.

nodes.label: Regression + trees
nodes.detail: Compare regularized regression with a constrained tree ensemble. Model complexity should follow available independent participants and outcome reliability.

nodes.label: Nested validation
nodes.detail: Keep each participant within one fold and reserve future measurements. Report error, calibration and subgroup performance; do not use test data to tune the model.

nodes.label: Nutrition-support trial
nodes.detail: Use the benchmark to define a support strategy, then test that strategy separately. Random assignment is needed to estimate its effect on the prespecified diet outcome.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Can baseline measures predict later diet quality well enough to guide a support study?
Design & unit
Prospective participant-level study for prediction; a subsequent randomized support trial is a separate phase.
Measures & analysis
Retain validated scoring and timing, compare simple and nonlinear models, then assess future-outcome prediction.
Data & sample
Requires raw scale responses, repeated outcomes, consent and a data dictionary. Plan participant count against model complexity, outcome variance and attrition.
Decision gate
Advance only if prediction adds useful information over the baseline. Predictive importance does not identify an intervention effect.

study.title: Policy packages, preferences and acceptance
study.summary: The model accounts for both the package and differences between respondents.

nodes.label: Restrictions + support
nodes.detail: Packages combine restrictions with grants, public transport, fares and reinvestment measures. Values refer to the supplied policy-choice specification.

nodes.label: Dependence + context
nodes.detail: The reported interaction analysis includes motorcycle dependence, income, environmental concern and trust. These are preference differences, not randomized personal traits.

nodes.label: Policy-choice model
nodes.detail: Estimate how package features change stated choices. The project materials report n = 320 and ρ² = 0.28; a full estimation file is not available here.

nodes.label: Monthly WTP
nodes.detail: Convert model coefficients relative to cost into VND per month. Positive support values and negative restriction values describe stated trade-offs.

study.legend: Arrows show the analysis sequence, not causal effects.

next.title: Test the transition before scaling it
next.summary: Separate a richer preference model from an evaluation of actual policy support.

nodes.label: Recover choice data
nodes.detail: Recover the task design, coding and respondent identifiers. Reproduce the interaction and willingness-to-pay estimates before adding model complexity.

nodes.label: Mixed / latent class
nodes.detail: Compare continuous and discrete preference variation with the existing specification. Do not assign additional classes without stable fit and interpretable profiles.

nodes.label: District holdout
nodes.detail: Test packages in independently sampled districts and income groups. Keep uncertainty visible for groups with limited coverage.

nodes.label: Support-package pilot
nodes.detail: Evaluate a feasible support measure using a prespecified comparison. Observe uptake, travel costs and mode use; do not read simulated acceptance as actual compliance.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Which support package remains acceptable across districts, and does it change observed travel behavior?
Design & unit
Preference replication followed by a district-aware pilot; the assignment and comparison design must be set before intervention.
Measures & analysis
Compare model stability and subgroup uncertainty, then estimate a separate pilot contrast on observed uptake or travel behavior.
Data & sample
Requires task data, district sampling information and new pilot observations. Plan for district clustering, subgroup precision and attrition.
Decision gate
Keep predicted preference and observed uptake separate. Policy-effect claims require a defensible comparison and assumptions.

study.title: Semantic mapping meets asymmetric effects
study.summary: The language model identifies attributes; PRCA distinguishes reward from penalty.

nodes.label: Hotel reviews
nodes.detail: Project materials report 97,014 reviews from approximately 1,000 properties. Retain the review score as a separate outcome.

nodes.label: Sentence-BERT
nodes.detail: Use sentence embeddings to map review text to eight service attributes. Embedding similarity is a mapping signal; it is not the review rating itself.

nodes.label: Negative sentiment
nodes.detail: Construct the negative attribute indicators used in the regression. A penalty coefficient describes a score association when the negative indicator is present.

nodes.label: Positive sentiment
nodes.detail: Construct positive attribute indicators separately. Reward and penalty need not be equal in size or opposite in sign.

nodes.label: PRCA + Kano
nodes.detail: Compare OLS coefficients with HC1 robust standard errors, then classify service attributes. The reported R² = 0.220 describes fit to the supplied sample.

study.legend: Arrows show the analysis sequence, not causal effects.

next.title: Check the language model before ranking services
next.summary: Develop annotation, uncertainty and transfer checks around the existing PRCA analysis.

nodes.label: Attribute + sentiment
nodes.detail: Label a stratified review subset. Audit attribute mapping and polarity separately, including mixed-sentiment and ambiguous sentences.

nodes.label: Embedding benchmark
nodes.detail: Compare the current mapping with a multilingual encoder or supervised classifier. Reuse the same labelled evaluation split; do not choose a model from attractive examples.

nodes.label: PRCA + dependence
nodes.detail: Assess whether findings survive alternative sentiment thresholds and dependence within properties. Compare property-clustered uncertainty with the reported HC1 specification.

nodes.label: Later-period check
nodes.detail: Reserve later reviews and new properties. Examine whether priority rankings remain stable before linking the analysis to service investment.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Do service priorities survive annotation error, property dependence and a later review period?
Design & unit
Review-level reanalysis with property identifiers and a reserved temporal sample.
Measures & analysis
Report mapping and sentiment errors, coefficient intervals, threshold sensitivity and ranking stability. Keep mapping quality separate from regression fit.
Data & sample
Requires sentence-level labels, rating data, property IDs and collection dates. Size the annotation set for rare attributes as well as frequent ones.
Decision gate
Recommend a priority only when the direction and practical size remain stable. Investment returns require a separate service evaluation.

study.title: From themes to service hypotheses
study.summary: This map is an interpretation framework linked to the segmentation study.

nodes.label: Review themes
nodes.detail: Start with recurring themes from the Da Nang review analysis. This framework does not add an independent dataset.

nodes.label: Comfort + care
nodes.detail: Connect room comfort and service care to possible guest priorities. These dimensions provide an interpretation vocabulary, not estimated importance weights.

nodes.label: Local experience
nodes.detail: Connect food, location and ambience with what guests seek during a stay. Avoid assigning the same priority to every guest group.

nodes.label: Overall value
nodes.detail: Relate price and the overall stay to value judgments. A theme alone does not identify willingness to pay.

nodes.label: Service hypotheses
nodes.detail: Translate themes into service or messaging options to test. A plausible guest story remains a hypothesis until measured.

study.legend: Arrows represent interpretation steps, not estimated structural paths.

next.title: Turn the value framework into measurable constructs
next.summary: Use qualitative work to define the dimensions before estimating a structural model.

nodes.label: Guest interviews
nodes.detail: Ask guests what comfort, care and local experience mean in actual stays. Purposefully sample contrasting profiles; retain a transparent coding record.

nodes.label: Items + pilot
nodes.detail: Write candidate items from the definitions and existing scales. Check content coverage, translation and comprehension before statistical screening.

nodes.label: CFA + invariance
nodes.detail: Collect an independent survey to test measurement structure and comparability. EFA may precede CFA if the dimensions remain uncertain.

nodes.label: Value → stay outcome
nodes.detail: Test whether the measured dimensions relate to satisfaction or return intention. Observed repeat stays would require permissioned longitudinal records.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Are the proposed value dimensions distinct, understandable and comparable across guest groups?
Design & unit
Sequential qualitative instrument development and an independent guest survey.
Measures & analysis
Document definitions and item origins, evaluate measurement structure, then test a bounded association with a prespecified stay outcome.
Data & sample
Requires interviews, pilot feedback and new survey data. Plan qualitative coverage and quantitative precision separately; no new sample is claimed.
Decision gate
Use a structural model only after the measurement is defensible. Numerical weights and loyalty effects remain unestimated.

study.title: Measurement first, structural paths second
study.summary: EFA uses 200 responses; CFA and SEM use the remaining 365.

nodes.label: Content experience
nodes.detail: Content experience is one of the three modeled antecedents of consumer engagement. Its scale captures the survey construct defined in the manuscript.

nodes.label: Expectation alignment
nodes.detail: Evaluate the correspondence between expected and experienced content. The original items are needed to reproduce its measurement.

nodes.label: Brand equity transfer
nodes.detail: Model the brand-related construct as a separate engagement antecedent. Its path is not an observed commercial uplift.

nodes.label: Consumer engagement
nodes.detail: SEM examines the direct and mediated relationships. The reported 55% refers to explained variance, not a percentage increase in engagement.

nodes.label: Customer retention
nodes.detail: The reported 70% refers to explained variance in the modeled construct. Survey retention measures do not establish logged repeat visits.

study.legend: Arrows show hypothesized structural relationships; cross-sectional SEM does not establish causal direction.

next.title: Follow engagement into observed return behavior
next.summary: Extend the survey model with time ordering and permissioned behavioral data.

nodes.label: Repeated survey
nodes.detail: Measure antecedents before engagement and later return outcomes. Check whether the constructs retain comparable meaning across waves.

nodes.label: Return events
nodes.detail: With consent, join survey responses to defined return events. Specify an observation window and distinguish a revisit from an engaged return.

nodes.label: SEM + return model
nodes.detail: Use longitudinal SEM for the construct pathway and a prespecified binary or survival model for return events. An ML benchmark is optional when data volume supports it.

nodes.label: Future-period test
nodes.detail: Evaluate the return model on a later period, with people kept separate across training and evaluation. Report attrition and uncertainty in the longitudinal paths.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Does earlier measured engagement predict later observed return behavior?
Design & unit
Consent-based longitudinal panel with participant-linked return events.
Measures & analysis
Evaluate measurement comparability, temporal structural relationships and future return prediction as distinct outputs.
Data & sample
Requires scale items, linked events, consent and a follow-up plan. Sample rationale must account for events, attrition and the proposed longitudinal model.
Decision gate
Do not call the mechanism causal without additional identification. Logged behavior and the original retention construct must be reported separately.

study.title: Menu order, intended intake and tier choice
study.summary: The two studies address different outcomes; perceived value is the reported mediation pathway.

nodes.label: Menu ordering
nodes.detail: Participants see menu options and price tiers in different orders. The source describes two stated-preference experiments, with n = 257 and n = 147.

nodes.label: Intended calories
nodes.detail: Compare estimated intended intake across menu conditions. This is not weighed food consumption or measured plate waste.

nodes.label: Perceived value
nodes.detail: The reported indirect-effect analysis examines perceived value. Interpretation depends on mediation assumptions as well as randomized presentation.

nodes.label: Higher-tier choice
nodes.detail: The reported odds ratio is 0.52. Odds, choice probability and premium share are different quantities; the study reports them separately.

study.legend: Arrows summarize contrasts and the mediation specification; the mediator itself was not randomized.

next.title: Move from intended choice to restaurant behavior
next.summary: Test the menu intervention where diners order and eat.

nodes.label: Menu randomization
nodes.detail: Randomize menu versions at a practical unit such as a session or table. Prevent exposure to both versions and document implementation failures.

nodes.label: Orders + plate waste
nodes.detail: Record ordered tier, food served and food left using a consistent protocol. Define how estimated calories and waste are measured.

nodes.label: Multilevel contrasts
nodes.detail: Account for diners nested in the randomization unit. Prespecify the primary nutrition or waste outcome and a commercial guardrail such as spend.

nodes.label: Balance health + spend
nodes.detail: Use effect intervals and the commercial guardrail to decide whether to retain the menu order. A subgroup model is exploratory unless powered and prespecified.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Does healthier-first ordering change actual intake or waste without an unacceptable commercial trade-off?
Design & unit
Field experiment with the randomization unit fixed before recruitment.
Measures & analysis
Observe consumption or waste and spending; estimate contrasts with dependence at the assignment unit.
Data & sample
Requires restaurant cooperation, consistent measurement and participant information. Plan sample size from a meaningful primary effect, clustering and implementation loss.
Decision gate
Set the acceptable commercial trade-off before the trial. Do not substitute intended calories for observed consumption.

study.title: Individual and shared ownership
study.summary: A conceptual framework for relationships to test in an organizational setting.

nodes.label: Control + identification
nodes.detail: The framework links control over work, identification and responsibility with a felt ownership connection. The current source does not provide an estimated measurement model.

nodes.label: Individual ownership
nodes.detail: A felt sense that a work target is mine. It is distinct from legal ownership and from a verified claim of higher performance.

nodes.label: Collective ownership
nodes.detail: A shared sense that the target is ours. Team-level meaning requires a justified measure and aggregation; it cannot be assumed from one person's answer.

nodes.label: Commitment
nodes.detail: The framework proposes commitment as a link to cooperative behavior. No coefficients, sample or confirmed mediation test are supplied.

nodes.label: Cooperation
nodes.detail: Define observable cooperative behavior before collecting data. This conceptual endpoint does not establish employee retention or teaching improvement.

study.legend: Arrows represent proposed relationships. No structural coefficients have been estimated.

next.title: Build the measures before testing the pathway
next.summary: Develop a setting-specific ownership study with individual and team levels kept distinct.

nodes.label: Interviews + definitions
nodes.detail: Identify the ownership target and who shares it. Interview contrasting roles before selecting or adapting items.

nodes.label: Items + pilot
nodes.detail: Check comprehension and content coverage for individual ownership, collective ownership, commitment and cooperation.

nodes.label: Independent CFA
nodes.detail: Test distinctness and uncertainty in an independent sample. A good fit index alone does not establish valid measurement.

nodes.label: Team structure
nodes.detail: Examine whether a shared ownership construct supports aggregation. Use a multilevel design only with enough independent teams.

nodes.label: Longitudinal pathway
nodes.detail: Measure ownership before commitment and cooperation. Evaluate alternative explanations and report associations unless a stronger identification strategy is available.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
How do individual and shared ownership relate to later commitment and cooperation in a defined workplace?
Design & unit
Qualitative adaptation, independent measurement study and a longitudinal employee panel; teams are a possible second level.
Measures & analysis
Specify the ownership target, audit item meaning, test measurement structure and justify aggregation before structural modeling.
Data & sample
Requires a named setting, access, new measures and consent. Plan employees and independent teams separately, including attrition.
Decision gate
Do not estimate a team model without adequate team-level information. The existing page remains a conceptual framework.

study.title: Experience value, attitude and intention
study.summary: Measurement checks precede the reported PROCESS Model 4 mediation analysis.

nodes.label: Learning value
nodes.detail: Evaluate the learning component of the workshop experience. The project reports a 0.35 learning-to-attitude path, without enough detail to label it standardized.

nodes.label: Social value
nodes.detail: Represent the social component separately from learning and enjoyment. The experience dimensions connect with intention through the workshop-attitude pathway.

nodes.label: Hedonic value
nodes.detail: Represent enjoyment as a distinct experience dimension. The reported model connects this value with attitude toward the workshop.

nodes.label: Workshop attitude
nodes.detail: PROCESS Model 4 examines an indirect pathway through attitude. The project reports an attitude-to-intention path of 0.59.

nodes.label: Participation intention
nodes.detail: The source reports 216 valid responses in Melbourne. Intention is not an observed booking or repeat-attendance outcome.

study.legend: Arrows summarize the tested pathway; coefficients are not relabeled as standardized or causal.

next.title: Test an experience change against actual booking
next.summary: Move from a mediation model to a small, measurable service experiment.

nodes.label: Guided-learning format
nodes.detail: Define one teachable change, such as structured beginner guidance. Match the comparison workshop on duration, price and basic materials.

nodes.label: Workshop assignment
nodes.detail: Randomize a feasible unit such as a session. Record who receives the format and avoid mixing conditions within a shared session.

nodes.label: Booking + experience
nodes.detail: Measure learning experience and attitude separately from bookings or repeat attendance. Set a consistent follow-up window.

nodes.label: Primary contrast
nodes.detail: Estimate the randomized contrast on the prespecified booking outcome. Examine mediation secondarily with explicit assumptions and session-level dependence.

next.legend: Proposed workflow. No new data or model results are claimed.
plan: Question
Does structured beginner guidance improve actual booking or repeat attendance?
Design & unit
Session-aware experiment with a defined follow-up period and a matched comparison.
Measures & analysis
Preregister a behavioral primary outcome, retain experience measures as secondary outcomes and account for session dependence.
Data & sample
Requires new workshop delivery, participant information and permissioned booking records. Plan sessions and participants against a meaningful effect and attrition.
Decision gate
Keep the service change only if the behavioral contrast supports it. The original intention model does not establish this effect.
